factual_methodological.summary: Central observations were revalidated against the September 25 Census durable-goods release, official U.S. Treasury nominal and real yield curves, the final University of Michigan September survey, and current Reuters reporting. Core capital-goods orders rose 1.6%, shipments 0.6%, the official September 25 10-year/30-year yields were 5.17%/5.49%, real 10-year/30-year yields were 2.83%/3.22%, and consumer sentiment was 48.1 with one-year inflation expectations at 4.6%. The Saturday political update was refreshed before approval: Trump publicly rejected Iran's Hormuz proposal, so Friday's oil relief is not presented as an agreed reopening path.

taxonomy.summary: The daily remains inside political-economy-markets with the fixed global-macro classification, controlled dimensions, geography, topics, war-armed-conflict phenomenon, brief format and daily cadence.

translation.summary: EN/PT-BR preserve the same thesis, numbers, causal sequence, Saturday Hormuz update and visual values. Raw PT-BR uses natural equivalents for throughput/capex where those terms had no editorial need.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Opening leads with the new equipment-investment/expensive-capital divergence, headings state mechanisms rather than template fields, the prose exposes no QA process, and the conclusion synthesizes contrary evidence and forward variables.

contextual_depth.summary: The daily uses durable context only where it explains transmission: high real yields select among investment projects; household expectations constrain easing; and Gulf diplomacy is explicitly separated from physical shipping normalization.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 analytical table + 1 explicit business-equipment chart + 1 causal flow in each locale
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Both locales meet the brief floor with identical values and compatible units. The chart uses observed August month-on-month values and the flow distinguishes the investment/interest-rate channel from the Gulf energy-risk channel.

novelty_repetition.summary: Compared with the three prior public MT-GM editions, the dominant new information is the September 25 release showing 1.6% core capital-goods orders and 0.6% shipments under a >5% long-rate regime. The Saturday U.S. rejection of Iran's proposal is an additional material update to the energy tail; long yields and equity resilience are supporting context rather than a recycled lead thesis.

political_neutrality.summary: Contested geopolitical claims and motives are attributed. The report states the observable U.S. rejection and Iranian proposal terms without endorsing either side or inferring political motives as fact.

contrary_evidence: Headline durable-goods orders were virtually unchanged in August, so the manufacturing signal is not uniformly strong.
Regional Federal Reserve surveys cited in contemporaneous reporting showed some moderation in capital-expenditure plans despite strong realized core orders.
Consumer sentiment weakened while inflation expectations rose, arguing against a painless broad investment boom.

Equities rose and oil fell on Friday, evidence against a uniform financial-tightening narrative; Saturday's rejection of the Iranian proposal also means Friday's energy relief cannot be assumed durable.
limitations: Friday market prices precede the Saturday U.S. rejection of Iran's Hormuz proposal; the next market session may reprice the energy and rates channels.
The relationship between AI investment, Treasury yields and equity resilience is analytical inference rather than a fully identified causal decomposition.
University of Michigan inflation expectations are survey expectations, not realized inflation.
Strong core capital-goods orders may be concentrated in technology-linked categories and do not establish a broad-based productivity cycle.
notes: QA was rerun after the Saturday Hormuz fact changed. The stale 'awaiting U.S. response' language was removed before approval. Public-state recheck at reviewed HEAD found no canonical bundle or data/reports.json entry for MT-GM-2026-09-26. Approval is bound to the exact current pending and EN/PT-BR blobs.

en.title: Global Macro — Strong U.S. equipment demand collides with a 5% long-rate regime
en.deck: August capital-goods orders show a resilient U.S. equipment-investment cycle even as long real and nominal yields remain restrictive and household inflation expectations rise.
en.regime: Selective investment strength under expensive capital: equipment demand remains firm while long real and nominal yields stay restrictive and household confidence weakens.
en.key_risk: Persistent high real yields could spread financing pressure beyond housing and weaker borrowers, while the U.S. rejection of Iran's Hormuz proposal leaves the energy-inflation tail exposed to renewed escalation.
watch: Breadth of U.S. equipment investment beyond AI-linked categories
U.S. 10-year and 30-year nominal and real yields
Credit spreads, issuance quality and project cancellations
Any renewed U.S.-Iran diplomatic channel and verified Hormuz throughput, freight and insurance conditions

novelty_gate.dominant_delta: The August durable-goods release arrived after the September 25 daily: core U.S. capital-goods orders rose 1.6% and shipments 0.6%, showing realized equipment-investment strength even as official 10-year and 30-year Treasury yields closed at 5.17% and 5.49%. A second same-day update materially changes the energy tail: Trump publicly rejected Iran's proposal to reopen Hormuz after Friday's oil relief.
novelty_gate.repetition_control: The report does not reuse high long yields or equity resilience as the lead. It treats them as the financing environment for the newly observed capital-goods/household divergence. Gulf diplomacy is explicitly updated through Saturday's U.S. rejection and kept separate from verified physical normalization.
